article_context: The body image illustrates Error No. 5, slow and interrupted pouring: uneven setting can leave a cracked floor that must be broken out and redone. The animation should emphasize the visible structural failure rather than introduce a new construction step.
image_reading: A severely damaged concrete floor has been partly broken out, with a large loose slab, deep cracks, rubble, dust, and demolition tools visible.
The central cracked slab and surrounding debris are the clearest movable elements; a small amount of crumbling and settling is physically plausible while the tools remain still.

models.positive_prompt: A crack slowly extends across the central loose floor slab as its edge crumbles and settles slightly, releasing a small trickle of dust and grit. Fixed camera; by the final frame the longer open crack and displaced edge are clearly visible.
models.scene_plan: Over five seconds, keep the camera fixed on the central broken slab. The existing crack gradually propagates toward the slab edge at a steady, restrained pace; tiny fragments and dust loosen along the same fracture while the slab settles by a few millimeters. End with the crack visibly longer and more open and the weakened edge slightly displaced, with all tools and the broader demolition scene unchanged.

models.positive_prompt: The existing fracture creeps steadily through the central slab while small crumbs and dust fall into the gap. Keep the camera fixed; end with the slab edge slightly lower and the crack visibly extended.
models.scene_plan: Use the full five-second shot for one gradual failure process. With a fixed camera, let the main fracture creep through the loose central section as fine debris intermittently drops into the gap and the unsupported edge eases downward. The motion slows naturally near the end, leaving a clearly extended fracture and a modestly lowered slab edge.

models.positive_prompt: The central floor crack spreads a short distance as the loose edge sinks slightly and sheds fine dust into the gap. Fixed camera; finish on the widened fracture and settled slab edge.
models.scene_plan: For four seconds, hold the camera still and focus tightly through motion on the central fracture. Begin the crack extension immediately, keep its travel short and readable, and pair it with a slight downward settling of the same loose edge and a brief fall of fine dust. Reach the final widened fracture and settled edge close to the end without moving the tools or changing the damaged-floor context.

structured_intent.editorial_meaning: Interrupted or excessively slow pouring can cause uneven hardening, cracking, and costly removal of the failed floor.
structured_intent.primary_action: The existing fracture propagates through the loose central floor slab as its weakened edge crumbles and settles.
structured_intent.semantic_invariant: The floor remains visibly failed and under demolition, reinforcing the consequence of an improper interrupted pour.
structured_intent.terminal_state: The central crack is visibly longer and more open, with the adjacent slab edge slightly displaced and fresh grit in the gap.
